Learned 87T relays are rarely compared on common data and folds. We evaluate on simulated 300\,MVA and 40\,MVA plants with trace-grouped cross-validation (3 seeds $\times$ 5 folds, 3,302 traces) and re-implement six published methods. Natively, none reaches 93\,\% dependability with 98.8\,\% security; the two most dependable reach 97.0\,\% and 96.5\,\% at 75.3\,\% and 82.9\,\% security. A dual-path supervisory logic (87T-gated classifier, classifier-alone path, high-set) accepts any classifier. With equal search and epoch budgets, six instances reach 93.5-$-$95.7\,\% dependability and 98.8-$-$99.9\,\% security. A harmonic-restrained 87T tuned on validation traces over an extended grid (post-hoc; 92.8\,\% / 98.9\,\%) cannot be told apart from the deployed LSTM instance (93.0\,\% / 99.0\,\%; trace-clustered test, $p_{\mathrm{H}}=$\,1.00 on both metrics) and detects more high-impedance faults (69.9\,\% against 65.4\,\%). Four of six instances are more dependable than this relay, by 1.3-$-$3.0 points (post-hoc, Holm-adjusted), and none is less secure. Tuning alone raised the harmonic 87T from 86.0\,\% (textbook) to 92.8\,\% dependability, by 6.8 points, more than any classifier gains over the tuned relay (at most 3.0). Zero-shot security on the unseen plant is 99.9\,\% with Key's network but 88.4\,\% with the deployed LSTM, whose classifier-alone path caused 87 of 89 false trips; the frozen tuned relay reaches 96.8\,\% / 99.1\,\%. The deployed LSTM relay does not outperform a well-tuned conventional relay; the benchmark, the reproductions and the classifier-agnostic logic are the contribution.
